name: Non-amyloid Monoclonal Immunoglobulin Deposition Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Monoclonal Immunoglobulin Deposition Disease

criteria.description: Demonstration of non-amyloid monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits in tissue biopsy by immunofluorescence or immunohistochemistry
Presence of circulating monoclonal immunoglobulin or light chains in serum or urine
Evidence of organ dysfunction consistent with immunoglobulin deposition (e.g., renal impairment, cardiomyopathy)
Exclusion of amyloid deposits by Congo red staining and electron microscopy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (histopathological confirmation, monoclonal protein detection, and organ dysfunction) must be met with exclusion of amyloidosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires tissue biopsy confirmation and exclusion of systemic amyloidosis.

laboratory: Serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis showing monoclonal immunoglobulin
Elevated serum free light chains with abnormal kappa/lambda ratio
Proteinuria with nephrotic range on urinalysis
Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen indicating renal impairment
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or increased echogenicity
MRI or CT may show organomegaly or tissue infiltration
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; disease associated with plasma cell dyscrasia
other: Renal biopsy with immunofluorescence demonstrating linear monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits along basement membranes
Electron microscopy showing granular non-fibrillar deposits

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of Congo red positive amyloid deposits with apple-green birefringence
Tubular casts composed of light chains causing acute kidney injury
Absence of linear basement membrane deposits
Presence of monoclonal protein without organ damage

redFlags: Evidence of systemic organ involvement beyond kidneys
